Change has been successfully rebased and submitted as 1aa94df4cb3b7ab864a4c5fb009538c259c2801e

Duplicate of https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/79150

and doesn't account for the problems in that patch.
We now use PDI `xyz.openbmc_project.Telemetry.Report` for PeakReading.
That doesn't fix the problem with Resets and being modeled on DBus

Implementing the Reset PATCH operation requires additional infrastructure in dbus-sensors app since it involves sending a MCTP VDM command to the device to perform the reset and hence this patch is only limited to GET operation support for PeakReading. Is it ok to implement Reset action support for PeakReading in a separate patch?

> Is it ok to implement Reset action support for PeakReading in a separate patch?

No, because that would mean merging this patch that violates the redfish spec.

And to be clear, yes I understand the complexity.  We cannot be checking in things that are incorrect.  There's also further complexity in that Reset is not per-sensor.

If we want to define a new property that DOESN'T have that requirement, we could.
Added the clarification on ResetMetrics action support in the commit message.
Done
Unpacking like this doesn't track.  We're using the sensor path to unpack a metric report definition?
Not the definition, but the metric report, which is at the same object path as Sensor.Value since dbus-sensor app itself is providing the metric report which is obtained directly from the device.
Done
nit, don't use auto here.
Done
Code looks correct now.  Waiting on pdi.
Ack.
I don't see anything wrong with this but where is the link to phosphor-dbus-interfaces/ ?

It uses xyz.openbmc_project.Telemetry.Report PDI - https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Telemetry/Report.interface.yaml.

I have mentioned the use of PDI in commit message. If you want I can also add link to this PDI in commit message.

Okay so it uses Readings from https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Telemetry/Report.interface.yaml#L46 
Is there anything that defines this Reading further? Is there anything that defines what id can be? I see id == "PeakReading" in the code. I am reading that PDI and I kind of would expect something around "PeakReading"

Based on my review of the PDIs, the possible values for `MetricId` are not documented. In this case, we set it to `PeakReading` because it represents a statistical report of the sensor value and matches the name of the Readfish property we are enabling.
Done
Anyway we can document this PeakReading  in PDI ?

I think Gunnar raises a good point. "PeakReading" is not a Metric ID so I don't think this is the right way to use the PDI. We probably need to look at OperationType from the PDI. Let me make any changes needed to the backend dbus-sensors to do the same and then this patch also needs to be reworked accordingly.
@haghera@nvidia.com please see https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/84651.
This patch now populate PeakReading property if OperationType is set to Maximum.
Is this documented in PDI now?

OperationType was always in the Telemetry PDI @gunnar@gmills.xyz. What documentation are you looking for?

Mapping OperationType::Maximum (Value) to PeakReading is obvious. And, we don't typically document D-Bus to Redfish mappings in the PDI?

> What documentation are you looking for?

Mention in the commit message OperationType. I didn't know this OperationType Max existed. 
https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/0814d6a59fbe7c7a3f7c3e4657441be3bcaa7d20/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Telemetry/Report.interface.yaml#L103

> And, we don't typically document D-Bus to Redfish mappings in the PDI?

Yep, agreed. I just want to make sure the PDI documentation exists to allow for another sensor app to do the same.
Makes sense, commit message is updated.

Updated the commit message to clarify that Property PeakReading is added if
OperationType in PDI property ReadingParameters is set to Maximum.
Resolving
Any unit tests needed here?
Unit tests are not needed.
I would say they are, at least for the free functions.
Added the test case for free function.
This method is already huge.  Please do not make it worse.  Break out things as needed into sub functions.
Done
I'm not in love with this backend dbus design, but the code does appear to follow PDI that exists, and matches Redfish.
